title: Lookup chunk 8 and a host-side thread-limit check
trigger: cuda5 gate 20261117-cuda5-gate-v3-all-01 failed in the fixture pass with the radix path forced for every k: 'too many resources requested for launch' at 1,024 threads (fixture random-1-w1-k10-t1024-m32).
cause: CUDA 12.6 compiles v3-all's radix instantiation of range_scores (commit 313e255) to 68 registers per thread; CUDA 13.3 on the laptop gave 55. A 1,024-thread block then needs 68 x 1,024 = 69,632 registers, more than the 65,536 per SM, so the launch fails. The laptop gate of v3-all ran the fixtures with the default crossover only, where no 1,024-thread fixture takes the radix path, so it did not show. The register growth comes from change 1's lookup holding one pending load per word for a chunk of 16 words in registers. The stats build of v3-all (70/75 registers) has the same limit; at the 256 threads used for timing every build launches.
fix_design: RBP_LOOKUP_CHUNK_WORDS default 16 -> 8 (owner decision 2026-11-17). New v3-1 and v3-all commits; ctrl, v3-2 and v3-3 commits are not touched.

Host check: after choosing the instantiation, cudaFuncGetAttributes(kernel).maxThreadsPerBlock; if SCORE_THREADS exceeds it, refuse with 'SCORE_THREADS <n> exceeds this kernel's limit of <m> threads per block (registers or launch bounds); use fewer threads' before any query is scored, instead of failing at launch.

Test hook: -DRBP_TEST_LAUNCH_BOUND=<n> adds __launch_bounds__(<n>) to range_scores; without it the macro is empty, so normal builds are unchanged. The fixture builds the scorer source with -DRBP_TEST_LAUNCH_BOUND=256 and expects the rejection at 1,024 threads (tests/check_range_bitpack.py --limit-scorer, run by gate_build.sh from the build's src/).
compile_probe: cuda5, CUDA 12.6, compile only: v3-all source with chunk 8 gives 42 (small-k) / 43 (radix) registers, no spills.
bugs_and_edge_cases_checked_in_design: Chunk 8 at 256 threads: a warp has up to 16 words (128 words / 8 warps), so warps with more than 8 words take a second set of search rounds; at most two chunks. 56 of the 500 calibration queries have more than 64 words. Lookup results are unchanged (same per-word interval search); the v3 lookup fixtures with 128 words at 256 and 32 threads cover multiple chunks.
The check reads attributes of the instantiation actually launched (radix or small-k), after the crossover decision.
Merge threads equal score threads (single kernel), so one check covers both.
cudaFuncGetAttributes failure is reported as an error, not ignored.
risks: Registers 42/43 round up to 48 per thread at allocation granularity: about 5 resident blocks per SM at 256 threads against 6 for ctrl (38 registers). To be reported to the owner before timing; not changed here.
The second chunk costs one more set of dependent load rounds for long queries.
The thread-limit check is host code only and does not change device SASS; the test hook changes SASS only when defined.
Parva's batched copy of range_scores and tests/check_batched_kernel_sync.py are not edited and will need a refresh.
tests: cuda5 re-gates of v3-1, v3-all, v3-all-clocks and v3-all-stats: fixtures with the v3 cases enforced, forced radix for every k including 1,024 threads (radix builds) and the thread-limit rejection fixture; 100K/1M x 500 calibration queries x k=10/100/1000 exact. The stats build skips the fixtures (each process needs a new statistics file, as registered) and runs the 100K/1M checks.
